news.title: Stocks Stumble Into CPI Day and Fed Week as September Scaries Arrive
news.summary:

- The energy complex remains a notable positive, but the broader market is experiencing a risk-off tilt as CPI and Fed considerations dominate near-term direction.

Bottom line (outlook): The S&P 500 faces increased downside risk into CPI and Fed decision week, with several indicators suggesting a potential continued September pullback. Unless inflation data or policy commentary shift risk sentiment, breadth remains weak and defensives may hold up better than cyclical names.

- Price move: Gold edged higher as the dollar weakened, with spot gold at $4,414.28/oz and December futures at $4,457.20 as of 0419 GMT.

  - Weaker U.S. dollar supports dollar-priced gold; the dollar remains subdued despite expectations for higher U.S. rates.

news.title: Gold, silver prices tumble as hot PPI lifts Fed-hike risk - Kitco AM Report | Kitco News

news.title: Gold Price Steadies Near $4,400, Silver Holds Above $66 as Markets Brace for a Fed Decision Complicated by War | India Infoline
news.summary:

- Key driver this week: Fed decision (Sept 15–16). Market pricing for a 25 bp rate hike sits around 60–65%, boosted by strong US payrolls and ADP jobs data. A rate hike raises non-yielding gold’s opportunity cost, pressuring prices.
- Key data inputs: US PPI (due later) and CPI (Friday). A soft/in-line CPI could raise expectations for a Fed hold and lift gold; a hotter core CPI would reinforce hike bets and weigh on gold.

- Near-term outlook: Short-term moves will hinge more on CPI/PPI and the Fed decision than longer-term fundamentals. A soft inflation print could bolster gold toward August highs; a hot print could push prices lower even as Gulf tensions persist.

news.title: Gold And Silver Tumble As September Rate Hike Appears More Likely

Bottom line for the gold price outlook: Upward pressure on rates (if inflation remains stubborn) tends to weigh on gold and silver in the near term, with oil volatility contributing additional downside risk. If Fed signals soften or inflation retreats, metal prices could stabilize or rebound.

news.title: EIA sees Brent near $90/bbl in second-half 2026 amid Middle East disruptions  | Oil & Gas Journal
news.summary:
Summary:

- The EIA’s September 2026 Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO) expects Brent crude to average about $90/barrel in H2 2026, about $8 higher than the August projection, with prices remaining elevated through end-2026 due to ongoing Middle East disruptions and constrained exports.
- Global crude inventories are tightening as oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb remain constrained. Disruptions include renewed Iranian export sanctions and attacks near the Bab el-Mandeb region, driving draws in global inventories (estimated 3.9 million b/d in Q2 2026; projected 3.0 million b/d in Q3 and 1.7 million b/d in Q4).
- Production disruptions: Middle East crude production shut-ins averaged 6.7 million b/d in August 2026, rising from 5.0 million b/d in July, with expectations of about 5.7 million b/d in Q4 2026. Saudi rerouting via the Suez Canal and ship-to-ship transfers are increasing costs and delivery timelines for Asian buyers.
- Outlook through 2027: Brent is forecast to ease to around $77/bbl by Q2 2027 as disruptions ease and inventories begin to rebuild, with a full-year 2027 average near $74/bbl, versus about $91/bbl in 2026. U.S. crude production is expected to rise from 13.8 million b/d in 2026 to 14.3 million b/d in 2027.

Key takeaway for macro analysis: Near-term crude prices remain elevated around $90/bbl due to Middle East disruption-induced supply tightness and inventory draws, but a gradual normalization is anticipated in 2027 as disruptions ease and production recovers.
